title: AI Jargon, Decoded
hook: Model, algorithm, LLM, GPT, training, parameters — the words get thrown around like everyone agrees what they mean. Here's the plain-English version.
key_points: A model is the trained thing that makes predictions; an algorithm is the recipe used to build it.
An LLM (large language model) is an AI trained on huge amounts of text to predict words.
GPT just means a particular family of LLMs — the 'G-P-T' is technical plumbing.
'Training' is the learning phase; 'parameters' are the dials it tunes — billions of them.
content_html: A lot of AI conversation is really just vocabulary you haven't been handed yet. Strip the mystique and most of the words are simple. A model is the trained thing that does the work — it takes an input and produces a prediction. An algorithm is the method used to create that model; think recipe (algorithm) versus the finished dish (model). Training is the learning phase where the model improves by example, and parameters are the internal dials it adjusts along the way — today's big models have billions of them.
extra_html: The brand names are less mysterious than they sound, too. An LLM — large language model — is just an AI trained on a huge amount of text whose core trick is predicting the next word; it's the engine inside chatbots. GPT refers to a specific family of these models, and the letters stand for technical design choices you don't need to memorize. You'll also hear generative (AI that creates content), prompt (what you type in), token (the chunks of text a model reads, roughly word-pieces), and inference (the model actually running to answer you, as opposed to being trained). None of it requires a computer-science degree — it's a small glossary doing a lot of intimidating.

related.title: What AI Actually Is
related.hook: AI isn't a thinking robot — it's software that learns patterns from huge piles of examples, then uses them to make a good guess about something new.

related.title: How AI Learns
related.hook: Training an AI is like teaching by flashcards on a massive scale: show it an example, let it guess, tell it how wrong it was, and nudge it to do better — billions of times.

related.title: Generative AI
related.hook: The AI behind ChatGPT and image generators doesn't look up answers — it predicts what plausibly comes next, one piece at a time, until it has built a whole response.

related.title: How a Language Model Works
related.hook: A chatbot isn't reading and thinking — it's running the world's most sophisticated autocomplete, picking each next word from probabilities learned across billions of sentences.

flashcards.prompt: What's the difference between a 'model' and an 'algorithm'?
flashcards.back_html: The algorithm is the recipe/method for learning; the model is the trained result that recipe produces and that actually makes predictions.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'LLM' stand for, in plain terms?

choices.text: Large language model — AI trained on lots of text to predict words
Logical learning machine — a robot that reasons
Low-level memory — a type of computer chip

flashcards.explanation_html: An LLM is a large language model: trained on enormous amounts of text, it works by predicting likely next words. Chatbots are built on LLMs.

flashcards.back_html: The internal dials the model tunes during training — modern models have billions of them. More parameters can mean more capability, at higher cost.
